newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end firmer in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end firmer in subdued trade.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended slightly firmer on Monday in subdued trade.
"The Euroyen futures market is consolidating before it tries to rally again," said a city bank dealer.
Another steep tumble in Japanese stocks on Monday failed to boost the September contract above its recent high of 99.36. Stock market woes had helped spur a rally early last week.

The Nikkei index closed down 609.70 points or 3.37 percent at 17,480.34 on Monday. Its session low of 17,237.27 was still above this year's low of 17,019.56 recorded a week ago, when September Euroyen futures rose to a high of 99.36.
"Falls in the stock market have been the sole reason recently for buying Euroyen futures. We need other reasons to buy further," said the city bank dealer.

Another dealer echoed this view. "A new rally may start if economic conditions on and after April 1 are as bad as have been expected (due to a tax hike) or if the Nikkei index slips below 17,020 or so."
The key September contract settled at 99.31 after opening at 99.28 and trading between 99.28 and 99.33, with 28,494 contracts changing hands.
An address this morning by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita to a two-day meeting of BOJ branch managers was neutral for the market, traders said.

Matsushita said the economy is continuing its gradual recovery and the strength of the recovery is gradually increasing. He also said that the BOJ was keeping a close watch on the economic impact of recent falls in Tokyo share prices.

"Matsushita's comments on the economy were more positive than before, which was a selling factor. But his remarks on stocks were unexpected because the BOJ often avoids talking about the stock market's fluctuations and this was a buying factor. Thus, the impact was neutral," said one dealer. Earlier the BOJ conducted a neutral money market operation as expected.
The key interbank overnight call rate was steady at 0.49 percent, underpinned by banks' repayment of a large amount of certificates of deposit (CDs) maturing on Monday, traders said.
Long-end benchmark three-month CDs were not issued, but were offered at an unchanged 0.53 percent.
